title: Intercalated Mullite Glass‐Ceramic Composites From Co‐Sintering of Aluminosilicate Glass and Kaolinite

abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The co‐sintering of kaolinite with varying contents of jadeite‐type (Jd) glass yields mullite‐containing glass‐ceramic composites with tunable properties, offering fine control over the crystallizing phases and residual glass content. The Jd glass phase drastically decreases the sintering temperature by instigating a liquid phase sintering.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Mullite crystallizes from kaolinite in the form of acicular grains, forming an interlocking structure throughout the whole glass matrix. This peculiar microstructure provides increased indentation fracture toughness to the glass‐ceramic composites, as well as exceptional structural stability at high temperature. The meticulous adjustment of the mullite to Jd glass ratio enables further refinement of their hardness and elastic properties.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>These architectured materials hold promise for applications in extreme environments, as well as in the fields of biomedicine and electronics.</jats:p>
journal: Journal of the American Ceramic Society
